shortName: Oregon Health & Science University School of Medicine
additionalCoursework:
There are no required pre-requisite courses for application to the Oregon Health & Science University School of Medicine. 

It is strongly recommended that applicants take a course in human anatomy and/or physiology. More information about our recommended premedical competencies can be found on our website: https://www.ohsu.edu/school-of-medicine/md-program/admissions

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The undergraduate medical education program developed a new method of teaching medical students about the ways that social, economic, legal, and cultural structures impact health. During the fall semester, a course explores how issues such as immigration, gender, trauma, substance abuse, and racism affect patient care. OHSU’s SOM is one of the few U.S. medical schools teaching this unique course led by medical students.  A faculty-taught companion course covers such areas as cultural competency and implicit bias. Second-year medical students choose the topics, design, and lead six small-group sessions required for all first-year students.

General information may be obtained by contacting the Center for Diversity & Inclusion at cdi@ohsu.edu or https://www.ohsu.edu/center-for-diversity-inclusion . Additional information relating to School of Medicine diversity and equity opportunities for learners can be found online at https://www.ohsu.edu/school-of-medicine/diversity-equity/learners .
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence, usually not to exceed 12 months, may be granted by the Associate Dean for Undergraduate Medical Education, to a student who finds it impossible to continue his or her education because of health or personal reasons. A leave of absence involves a complete withdrawal from course work for a designated period of time. The reason for the leave of absence must be resolved within the period of the leave.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Current students have membership at the March Wellness and Fitness Center. The center has a pool, class space, fitness equipment, as well as many personal wellness and fitness classes. Student organizations include The Alliance for Visible Diversity in Science (AVDS), Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association (APAMSA), Association of Native American Medical Students (ANAM), Latino Medical Student Association (LMSA), Middle Eastern and South Asian Association (MESAA), Students for LGBTQ Health, 
 American Medical Women's Association (AMWA), rural scholars, and more than 20 specialty-focused interest groups.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Students will spend their first 18 months in the Collaborative Life Sciences Building located on the South Waterfront Campus. University Hospital is located on a hilltop overlooking the city of Portland, Oregon.  Students have easy access to the city center as well as the surrounding communities.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On campus housing is not available; however, there are affordable apartments and other rental properties within a 5-mile radius.  The campus is also easily accessible via the OHSU Tram and public transportation.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
Opened in December 2019, the Health Justice Co-op (HJC) provides a safe space for students from marginalized communities, designed to foster collaborations that will advance justice in health care and education. The HJC was developed by students of color and of the LGBTQ community and faculty. The HJC space prioritizes diversity and justice-related programming and includes a health justice resources library, projector set up to display health justice films and documentaries, and an event calendar for students to stay connected to the community. 

The Students for LGBTQ Health group's mission is to provide safe, validating and inclusive health care and working environments at OHSU through education and advocacy.  Students for LGBTQ Health implements educational trainings, participates in community volunteer events and holds social gatherings and visibility campaigns. This group welcomes current and future health care professionals, gender and sexual minorities and allies.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Outreach, Advising, Support, and Identity formation for Students (OASIS) team provides a comprehensive system of support for medical students’ advising needs and their personal and professional identity formation throughout all years of medical school. Faculty Advisors work within the OHSU School of Medicine UME Program to provide academic, career, and life and wellness advising for medical students, create and deliver general support programming, and collaborate with a variety of individuals in UME and at the University to support the overall success of all medical students.

Our Life & Wellness Faculty Advisors provide a confidential venue for individual life and wellness advising to students.

Programming Events Include:

Successful transitioning into medical school
Personal relationships
Stress management
Financial wellness
Sleep, exercise, nutrition
Personal identity formation
Internal and external factors that influence personal identity formation
Accessing resources and skill development to foster fulfillment, success, and thriving as physicians of the future
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The OHSU School of Medicine is a vibrant community of educators, students, scientists, clinicians and others working side-by-side to heal, teach, discover and serve. We are proud of our uniquely collaborative and collegial environment.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The SOM Dean's Office provides free tutoring to students identified as needing assistance.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient interactions begin the first year of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Mix of active learning and lecture.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin Winter term of the second year of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance and punctuality are essential. Students seeking a predominantly online or at-home medical school foundational experience should seek admission at a different medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The OHSU M.D. Degree Program is competency-driven and learner-centered, and features integration of foundational and clinical sciences across all years. Active learning methods foster in-depth understanding and application of materials learned, while also facilitating development of skills needed for self-assessment, critical thinking, continual improvement, and life-long learning.

Early and longitudinal clinical experiences with physicians augment fundamental clinical knowledge and skills in patient interviewing, physical diagnosis, and communication skills in the Foundational curriculum. Assessment of student performance is multi-modal and competency-driven. Following this, students participate in core/elective clinical experiences in OHSU Hospitals and Clinics, as well as at our affiliated partner hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington, including rural settings.

More information online:  https://www.ohsu.edu/school-of-medicine/md-program/md-program-curriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Required clinical experiences in core disciplines of Family Medicine, Pediatrics, and Internal Medicine offer students exposure to and education in primary care fields.  All students are required to complete a rural clinical experience offered in a variety of disciplines during the clinical curriculum.  The Rural Scholars Program and global health experiences also provide opportunities for students interested in additional clinical immersion in these settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: OHSU is the recipient of a Clinical and Translational Science Award from NIH. Centered in the Oregon Clinical and Translational Research Institute (OCTRI), the program is designed to develop innovative solutions to improve the efficiency, quality and impact of the process for turning observations in the laboratory, clinic and community into interventions that improve the health of individuals and the public. OCTRI has an embedded research training program open to medical student participation. Students may apply to participate in the experience which provides training for those interested in careers in clinical and translational medical research and the opportunity to participate in mentored research activities. The program has five-month and one-year research options; students participating in the one-year option will earn a Master of Clinical Research degree. After completing the experience, students will have taken the first major step towards a career as a physician-scientist.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Scholarly Projects is an in-depth investigation of topics of interest to medical students with the goal of creating critical thinkers and lifelong learners.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: OHSU Hospital, Doernbecher, Veteran's Admin., Providence, Legacy, Kaiser Perm., Salem Hospital, Peacehealth, St. Charles, Asante Rogue, Willamette Valley, Tuality Community, Adventist, Unity Center
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass-No Pass for the Foundations of Medicine phase of the curriculum and for the Clinical Experiences phase of the curriculum.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Based in Portland, OHSU employs over 16,000 individuals, operates the top-ranked adult and children's hospitals in Oregon, and secures competitive research funding of more than $400 million a year. As a public organization, OHSU provides community outreach and services for Oregon's most vulnerable populations. OHSU includes the Marquam Hill, South Waterfront and West campuses. Overlooking the city of Portland, the Marquam Hill campus is connected to the South Waterfront by the Portland Aerial Tram. The Collaborative Life Sciences Building opened in 2014. It features classrooms and integrated spaces for students and faculty from OHSU, Portland State University, and Oregon State University. Altogether, OHSU occupies more than 7.8 million square feet of space on approximately 350 acres.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: It is the mission of the School of Medicine to enhance human health through programs of excellence in education, research, health care and public service to the larger community including underserved populations. In achieving these goals, the Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU) School of Medicine seeks to establish an educational environment that challenges its students to strive for academic excellence and fosters the development of compassion, humanism, professionalism, and cultural competence in the care of patients from their first days in the classroom to their final rotation in the hospitals and clinics. A fundamental priority throughout OHSU is to enable all students to fulfill their potential as human beings and as health care professionals while effectively meeting the health-related needs of the multiple communities they will serve.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes - those who are admitted will go through the background check process.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: It is recommended that at least one letter be from a science department teaching faculty member.  A letter packet containing at least three individual teaching faculty letters or a premedical committee evaluation report (Committee Letter) may be submitted in lieu of the three separate recommendations. Applicants who have been out of college for five years or more may submit two letters from employers and one from a teaching faculty member. It is highly recommended of all applicants that they provide additional non-academic recommendations as well.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Applicants should carefully select a well-chosen group of letters that speak to significant experiences in health care/physician shadowing and extracurricular accomplishments in addition to letters from three college or university teaching faculty from any department.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Details about the interview process for the 2026 application process will be posted on the OHSU UME Admissions website: https://www.ohsu.edu/school-of-medicine/md-program/admissions
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Multiple Mini Interview (MMI) Circuit as well as a one-on-one interview with a member of the Admissions Committee.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: No. But interview process is entirely virtual.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All verified applicants. We ask applicants to self-assess if they think they fit a mission based group
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Applicants who fit one or more of our mission based groups are given strong preference in the admissions process.

medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Applicants must be US citizens, have permanent residency with a valid Green Card, or have DACA status to be considered eligible.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The School of Medicine gives strong preference to the following applicants:

Residents of Oregon.

Non-resident applicants with Oregon Heritage. The School of Medicine uses the Oregon Heritage Policy for student selection, but it is not used as a basis for determining residency, and therefore the tuition a student pays. Oregon Heritage is defined as 1) A student with one or both parents residing in Oregon at the time of application, 2) A student who graduated from high school in Oregon with at least two years of attendance at a high school in Oregon, or 3) A student who graduated from any regionally accredited college or university in Oregon and attended at least two years at any regionally accredited college or university in Oregon no more than 7 years prior to the time of application.

Applicants who are WICHE-certified in Allopathic Medicine.

Applicants applying to the MD/PhD Combined Degree Program.

Applicants applying to the MD/MPH Combined Degree Program.

Non-resident applicants with superior achievements. Superior achievements are defined as significant experiences in healthcare, leadership, extracurricular activities, and/or community service activities.

Applicants with a demonstrated ability to overcome adversity and/or applicants who have personally experienced inequities within the healthcare system.

The School of Medicine Admissions Committee adheres to a policy of equal opportunity and non-discrimination on the basis of sex, age, race, ethnic origin, religion, disability, military service, sexual orientation, or any other status protected by law. The Committee also fully recognizes the importance of diversity in its student body and in the physician workforce in providing for effective delivery of health care. Accordingly, the OHSU School of Medicine strongly encourages applications from persons from all socioeconomic, racial, ethnic, religious, and educational backgrounds and from persons from groups underrepresented in medicine.

Please see the Admissions website for more detailed information regarding selection factors.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Interview screeners have access to all scores, but applicants must have a 497 or above on an eligible MCAT.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: An MCAT score of 497 or above taken in 2023-2026 is required for eligibility.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: A culumative total GPA (including any postbacc or graduate coursework) of 2.8 or above is required for eligibility.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: A culumative total GPA (including any postbacc or graduate coursework) of 2.8 or above is required for eligibility. There is no minimum GPA for undergraduate specifically.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent. There is no minimum number of credit hours.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept community college coursework toward our required GPA minimum.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Depending on where a file is in the process, updates may or may not have an effect on an application. The most impactful time for updates is at the time of scheduling an interview.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Graduates of the M.D. program need to be able to work in many different clinical situations and to provide a wide spectrum of care to patients.

To make sure our students have the leadership skills, knowledge and emotional maturity to function well on a medical team, OHSU and the School of Medicine have developed a set of technical standards.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Financial aid can be in the form of scholarships, grant-in-aid funding, workstudy, and loans.  Individual awards may vary depending on qualifications for funding.  For more information, please review the Web site at https://www.ohsu.edu/education/registrar-and-financial-aid

Please visit our scholarships page at https://www.ohsu.edu/school-of-medicine/md-program/scholarships-medical-students
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy:
The OHSU Board of Directors approved the OHSU Tuition Promise for students enrolled in eligible degree programs (including the M.D. program) starting in the 2013-14 academic year. These students will see no further increase in their tuition rate during the duration of their program, provided they complete their degree within the timeframe specified by their degree program. 

In addition, all first-year M.D. students who enrolled in the 2014-15 academic year as well as all first-year M.D. students enrolling in the 2015-16 academic year, will not see a tuition rate increase over their first year tuition rate during the duration of their M.D. program, provided they complete their degree within the timeframe specified by their program. For example, a new M.D. student entering in the 2015-16 academic year will incur the same tuition rate during the four-year length of their M.D. program.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The OHSU School of Medicine looks for proficiency in nine recommended categories, which encompass pre-professional, thinking and reasoning, and science competencies. Please go to the OHSU School of Medicine Undergraduate Medical Education Admissions website for more detailed information.

A course in anatomy is strongly recommended. Laboratories for biology, chemistry, and physics are recommended, but not required.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Coursework successfully completed by applicant does not expire.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The Admissions Committee seeks students who have demonstrated academic excellence and readiness for the profession of medicine and who will contribute to the diversity necessary to enhance the medical education of all students. Applicants are selected on the basis of demonstrated motivation for medicine, humanistic attitudes, and a realistic understanding of the role of the physician in providing excellent health care to all communities in need of care. 

Attention is paid to achievements that demonstrate breadth of interests and experiences, commitment to others, leadership, and ability to contribute diverse and innovative perspectives to problem-solving in medicine and healthcare. 

Evaluation of applicants includes the academic record, MCAT, letters of recommendation, volunteer and community service experiences, and interviews.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We recommend that applicants have experiences in a variety of clinical settings and medical practices.
